notes.sowing: Sow outdoors as soon as the soil can be worked, or start indoors 4 to 5 weeks before planting out. Press the seed onto the surface or barely cover it, as it needs light. Hardened-off plants can go out a week or two before your last frost.
notes.care: Grows in sun or part shade and copes with poor soil. Flowering slows in hot weather: shear plants back by half when nights cool to bring on new flowers. The small flowers are a rich nectar source for bees, hoverflies and tiny parasitic wasps.
notes.harvest: Flowers start 6 to 8 weeks from sowing and carry on until a hard frost, with a pause in midsummer heat. It is grown for edging, pots and beneficial insects rather than for cutting.
